story-040.manner: the whole passage is the patient's confession: hushed, hurried, frightened, breaking off at the ellipses, growing breathless towards the end; when he imitates his wife calling 'Misha!', do it softly, from a distance

story-041.manner: slow and low; a held breath before the raised hand

story-043.manner: very slow, almost a whisper, following the falling hand joint by joint

story-045.manner: the doctor shouts these words aloud in a measured, firm voice — loud and clipped, forcing himself to sound steady

story-046.manner: very quiet and slow, final; a long pause after 'He did not stir.'

story-001.manner: the opening: quiet and unhurried, with a trace of gentle irony at the young doctor he once was

story-007.manner: the patient's halting words: embarrassed, stumbling, real pauses at each ellipsis

story-013.manner: the patient: reluctant, then softly pleading

story-016.manner: the patient: timid and pleading; the words 'Leipzig… International Tournament, sir… Mate in three moves' spoken slowly, like a formula he has rehearsed

story-018.manner: the patient's long confession: quiet, hurried, passionate and frightened, breaking off at the ellipses; slowing down and becoming vivid as he describes the passers-by one by one

story-022.manner: the patient: lowered voice, a chill of dread; the last words 'a kind of terrible simplicity' almost breaking

story-024.manner: the patient: at first almost cheerful, then suddenly desperate

story-028.manner: the patient remembering the night garden: quiet and uneasy

story-029.manner: the patient thinking aloud: feverish and earnest, with a childlike pride, explaining the example of the number ten carefully

story-032.manner: the patient: faltering, then rushing, ending on a suspended 'if…'

story-037.manner: the patient: agitated, morbidly excited, rising almost to a cry at 'not fitted for it'

story-039.manner: the patient: morbid triumph, then grave and quiet
